title: Swelling above a dark front tooth

patient.name: Lina Haddad
patient.complaint: My front tooth hurts and the gum above it is swollen.
patient.opening: My front tooth is killing me and there's a lump on the gum above it. I can't even touch it.
patient.personality: worried about how her smile looks

topics.label: When it started
topics.answer: The throbbing started two days ago and the lump appeared yesterday.

topics.label: Past trauma
topics.answer: Now you mention it, I got hit in the mouth with a ball about five years ago. The tooth went a bit grey after that.

topics.label: Pain on biting
topics.answer: I can't bite on it at all, even touching it with my tongue hurts.

topics.label: Hot and cold
topics.answer: Cold doesn't bother it at all. Hot maybe makes the throbbing a little worse.

topics.label: Swelling
topics.answer: Just the lump on the gum above the tooth. My face isn't swollen and my eye is fine.

topics.label: Feeling unwell
topics.answer: I feel a bit tired but no fever. Swallowing and breathing are fine.

topics.label: Medical history
topics.answer: I'm allergic to penicillin. Otherwise healthy.

topics.label: Where exactly
topics.answer: Upper front, the one just left of the middle. The darker one.

items.question: Lina points to her upper front teeth, the darker one on her left. Click the tooth you would examine.
items.helper: Remember: her left is on your right when you face her.
items.explain: The upper left central incisor (21). On the 3D mouth, the patient's left is on your right in the front view.
items.reveal: 21 is grey compared with 11. There is a fluctuant swelling in the labial sulcus above it.

items.question: Which tests would help you most now? Select all that apply.
items.explain: Sensibility testing confirms the pulp has died, percussion shows periapical inflammation and the radiograph shows the periapical lesion.

findings.Cold test: No response on 21. 11 and 22 respond normally.
findings.Periapical radiograph: Periapical radiolucency at the apex of 21. The root canal is wider than on 11.
findings.Bite test: Too painful to do, and adds nothing here.

items.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.explain: A non-vital, discoloured tooth after old trauma, very tender to percussion, with a fluctuant swelling and a periapical radiolucency, is an acute apical abscess from pulp necrosis.

items.question: In one or two sentences, justify your diagnosis.
items.expected: The tooth is non-vital (no response to cold, grey after old trauma), very tender to percussion, and has a fluctuant swelling with a periapical radiolucency, so infection from the dead pulp has spread beyond the apex.

items.question: What is the best management?
options: Drain the abscess and start root canal treatment
answer: Drain the abscess and start root canal treatment
items.explain: Drainage through the canal or an incision, then root canal treatment, removes the source. Antibiotics are only an add-on if the infection spreads or she is systemically unwell, and she is allergic to penicillin.

items.question: What warning signs would you tell Lina to look out for after she leaves?
items.expected: Seek urgent help or go to the emergency department if the swelling spreads, especially towards the eye, if she gets a fever or feels very unwell, or if she has any difficulty swallowing or breathing.

teachingPoints: A grey tooth after old trauma is often non-vital.
Treat the source: drain and clean the canal. Antibiotics are only an adjunct for spreading infection.
Always give clear red-flag advice about spreading swelling and difficulty swallowing or breathing.
